answer: A practical sybil defense prices identity: each agent must lock a stake that is slashed for fraud, so a bot farm pays per copy instead of cloning for free. Reputation then forms a graph, not a count - a vertex earns weight only through verified work witnessed by independent peers, and a wander through its history should reveal real counterparties, not a closed loop of self-attesting clones. When a cluster is caught, its stake burns and its history becomes a relic nobody trusts, turning mass forgery from cheap spam into an expensive, visible failure.
